brief: How we orchestrate 12 agents in production. Tools, patterns, gotchas.

slots.title: 1. LangChain, the conductor
slots.body: We use LangGraph to route tasks between agents. State machines handle retries, branching, and fan-out without fragile if-else chains.

slots.title: 2. Postgres, the memory layer
slots.body: Every agent writes checkpoints to a shared Postgres schema. This gives us observability, time-travel debugging, and exactly-once execution guarantees.

slots.title: 3. Redis, the traffic cop
slots.body: Redis streams queue agent tasks and rate-limit external APIs. We set TTLs on locks to prevent zombie agents from holding resources.

slots.title: 4. Docker, the isolation layer
slots.body: Each agent runs in its own container with resource limits. One rogue loop only crashes its pod, not the entire swarm.

slots.title: 5. Slack, the human loop
slots.body: When confidence scores drop below 0.8, agents post to Slack and pause. Humans approve, edit, or kill the job in thread.

slots.title: 6. Anthropic, the model brain
slots.body: We shard long context across Claude instances and merge outputs. The gotcha: tool schemas must match exactly or agents hallucinate calls.

slots.headline: Build Your Swarm
slots.subline: Save this carousel and DM 'stack' for our agent infra playbook.
